```{r setup}
library(conflicted)
library(tidyverse)
library(powerjoin)
library(here)
library(synExtra)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(rtracklayer)

conflicts_prefer(
  dplyr::filter,
  dplyr::count,
  dplyr::slice,
  dplyr::rename,
  dplyr::select,
  dplyr::first,
  dplyr::desc,
  dplyr::between,
  dplyr::n,
  purrr::reduce,
  GenomicRanges::setdiff,
  GenomicRanges::intersect,
  GenomicRanges::union
)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Helvetica")
)

synapser::synLogin()
syn <- synDownloader(normalizePath("~/data"), .cache = TRUE)

data_dir <- here("dsrna", "data")
out_dir <- here("dsrna", "data", "cryptic_exon_te_overlap")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Loading data

### VOILA deltapsi LSVs

LSVs are all from Liu et al. data.

One row per LSV (module). Junction-level columns are `;`-separated, one
entry per junction. Coordinates are 1-based, closed, Ensembl chromosome names.

```{r}
lsv_raw <- syn("syn78075015") |>
  read_tsv(comment = "#", col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

lsv_raw
```

### RepeatMasker

Raw RepeatMasker `.out` table: 1-based closed coordinates, `C` = minus strand,
UCSC chromosome names. Converted to Ensembl naming to match MAJIQ / Ensembl GTF.

For plots and stuff only reall use the families of interesst.

```{r}
rmsk <- syn("syn55256576") |>
  read_csv(
    col_types = cols(
      sw_score = col_integer(), perc_div = col_double(),
      perc_del = col_double(), perc_ins = col_double(),
      start = col_integer(), end = col_integer(),
      id = col_integer(), .default = col_character()
    )
  ) |>
  select(-dummy) |>
  mutate(
    te_strand = if_else(strand == "C", "-", "+"),
    seqnames = str_remove(chromosome, "^chr") |>
      str_replace("^M$", "MT"),
    rep_class = str_remove(class_family, "/.*$"),
    rep_family = str_remove(class_family, "^[^/]*/?") |>
      na_if(""),
    te_id = row_number()
  )

rmsk_gr <- rmsk |>
  select(
    seqnames, start, end, strand = te_strand, te_id
  ) |>
  makeGRangesFromDataFrame(keep.extra.columns = TRUE)

repeat_whitelist <- tibble(
  class_family = c(
    "LINE/L1", "LINE/L2", "LTR", "LTR/ERV1", "LTR/ERVK", "LTR/ERVL",
    "LTR/ERVL-MaLR", "Retroposon/SVA", "SINE/Alu", "SINE/MIR"
  )
)
```

### Ensembl v113 exons

```{r}
ensembl_gtf_file <- file.path(data_dir, "Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gtf.gz")
if (!file.exists(ensembl_gtf_file)) {
  download.file(
    "https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-113/gtf/homo_sapiens/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gtf.gz",
    ensembl_gtf_file, method = "curl"
  )
}

annotated_exons <- readGFF(
  ensembl_gtf_file,
  filter = list(type = "exon"),
  tags = c("gene_id", "gene_name", "transcript_id", "transcript_biotype", "tag")
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    is_ensembl_canonical = map_lgl(tag, \(x) "Ensembl_canonical" %in% x)
  ) |>
  select(-tag)

annotated_exons |>
  count(is_ensembl_canonical)
```

Which annotated exons count as canonical for the subtraction. "all" removes
any exon annotated in any Ensembl transcript. "ensembl_canonical" only removes
exons from the single Ensembl canonical transcript per gene, so alternative but
annotated exons are retained as putative cryptic exons.

All makes more sense imho, we really only want cryptic unannotated exons.

```{r}
canonical_exon_set <- "all"

canonical_exons_gr <- annotated_exons |>
  filter(
    canonical_exon_set == "all" | is_ensembl_canonical
  ) |>
  select(seqnames = seqid, start, end, strand) |>
  makeGRangesFromDataFrame() |>
  GenomicRanges::reduce()

canonical_exons_gr
```

## Aggregate each LSV to its most changing junction

For every LSV, pick the junction with the highest probability of changing
(|dPSI| > 0.2, VOILA default) and report its dPSI and PSI values. Ties are
broken by larger |dPSI|.

```{r}
junction_cols <- c(
  "mean_dpsi_per_lsv_junction", "probability_changing",
  "probability_non_changing", "TDPneg_mean_psi", "TDPpos_mean_psi",
  "de_novo_junctions", "junctions_coords"
)

lsv_junctions <- lsv_raw |>
  select(lsv_id, all_of(junction_cols)) |>
  separate_longer_delim(all_of(junction_cols), delim = ";") |>
  group_by(lsv_id) |>
  mutate(junction_idx = row_number()) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        mean_dpsi_per_lsv_junction, probability_changing,
        probability_non_changing, TDPneg_mean_psi, TDPpos_mean_psi
      ),
      as.numeric
    ),
    de_novo_junctions = de_novo_junctions == "1"
  )

lsv_max <- lsv_junctions |>
  group_by(lsv_id) |>
  arrange(desc(probability_changing), desc(abs(mean_dpsi_per_lsv_junction))) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  rename(
    max_junction_idx = junction_idx,
    max_junction_coords = junctions_coords,
    max_junction_de_novo = de_novo_junctions,
    max_probability_changing = probability_changing,
    max_probability_non_changing = probability_non_changing,
    max_dpsi = mean_dpsi_per_lsv_junction,
    max_TDPneg_psi = TDPneg_mean_psi,
    max_TDPpos_psi = TDPpos_mean_psi
  ) |>
  power_left_join(
    lsv_raw |>
      select(
        lsv_id, gene_name, gene_id, lsv_type, num_junctions, num_exons,
        seqnames = seqid, strand, exons_coords
      ) |>
      mutate(
        gene_id = str_remove(gene_id, "^gene:"),
        # VOILA fills gene_name with the gene id when there is no symbol
        gene_name = if_else(str_starts(gene_name, "gene:"), NA, gene_name)
      ),
    by = "lsv_id",
    check = check_specs(
      unmatched_keys_left = "abort",
      duplicate_keys_right = "abort"
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    any_de_novo_junction = lsv_id %in% (
      lsv_junctions |> filter(de_novo_junctions) |> pull(lsv_id)
    )
  )

lsv_max

p <- ggplot(lsv_max, aes(max_dpsi, max_probability_changing)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.5) +
  labs(
    x = "dPSI TDP43- vs TDP43+ (most changing junction)",
    y = "P(|dPSI| > 0.2)"
  )

ggsave(
  file.path(out_dir, "liu_lsv_max_dpsi_vs_probability.pdf"),
  p, width = 6, height = 5
)
```

## Exons of each LSV

All exons belonging to the LSV, not just those touched by the most changing
junction. MAJIQ reports half-exons with an unknown boundary as `na`,
those can't be placed and are dropped.

```{r}
lsv_exons <- lsv_max |>
  select(lsv_id, seqnames, strand, exons_coords) |>
  separate_longer_delim(exons_coords, delim = ";") |>
  separate_wider_delim(
    exons_coords, delim = "-", names = c("start", "end")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    half_exon = start == "na" | end == "na",
    across(c(start, end), \(x) suppressWarnings(as.integer(x)))
  )

lsv_exons |>
  count(half_exon)

lsv_exons_gr <- lsv_exons |>
  filter(!half_exon) |>
  select(-half_exon) |>
  makeGRangesFromDataFrame(keep.extra.columns = TRUE)
```

## Subtract canonical exons

Strand-aware subtraction of the annotated exons from every LSV exon. What
remains are the putative cryptic exon segments. A single LSV exon can produce
multiple segments (e.g. an annotated exon with an unannotated extension on
both sides).

For min_cryptic_width, let's try 20bp.

```{r}
min_cryptic_width <- 20L

cryptic_segments_grl <- GenomicRanges::subtract(
  lsv_exons_gr, canonical_exons_gr, ignore.strand = FALSE
)

cryptic_per_lsv <- tibble(
  lsv_id = rep(lsv_exons_gr$lsv_id, lengths(cryptic_segments_grl)),
  lsv_exon_start = rep(start(lsv_exons_gr), lengths(cryptic_segments_grl)),
  lsv_exon_end = rep(end(lsv_exons_gr), lengths(cryptic_segments_grl)),
  as_tibble(unlist(cryptic_segments_grl, use.names = FALSE))
) |>
  mutate(
    across(c(seqnames, strand), as.character),
    # Is the whole MAJIQ exon unannotated, or only part of it
    # (alternative 5'/3' splice site extension)
    cryptic_type = if_else(
      start == lsv_exon_start & end == lsv_exon_end,
      "full_exon", "partial_exon"
    )
  ) |>
  filter(width >= min_cryptic_width)

cryptic_per_lsv |>
  count(cryptic_type)
```

Collapse identical cryptic segments shared between LSVs (the same exon is
typically part of both a source and a target LSV). Each unique cryptic exon
is annotated with the most changing LSV it belongs to.

```{r}
cryptic_exons <- cryptic_per_lsv |>
  power_left_join(
    lsv_max |>
      select(
        lsv_id, gene_name, gene_id, max_probability_changing, max_dpsi,
        max_TDPneg_psi, max_TDPpos_psi, max_junction_coords,
        max_junction_de_novo, any_de_novo_junction
      ),
    by = "lsv_id",
    check = check_specs(
      unmatched_keys_left = "abort",
      duplicate_keys_right = "abort"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(seqnames, start, end, strand, width) |>
  arrange(desc(max_probability_changing), desc(abs(max_dpsi))) |>
  summarize(
    n_lsvs = n_distinct(lsv_id),
    lsv_ids = paste(unique(lsv_id), collapse = ";"),
    gene_name = paste(unique(na.omit(gene_name)), collapse = ";"),
    gene_id = paste(unique(gene_id), collapse = ";"),
    cryptic_type = paste(sort(unique(cryptic_type)), collapse = ";"),
    any_de_novo_junction = any(any_de_novo_junction),
    best_lsv_id = first(lsv_id),
    best_probability_changing = first(max_probability_changing),
    best_dpsi = first(max_dpsi),
    best_TDPneg_psi = first(max_TDPneg_psi),
    best_TDPpos_psi = first(max_TDPpos_psi),
    best_junction_coords = first(max_junction_coords),
    best_junction_de_novo = first(max_junction_de_novo),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(seqnames, start) |>
  mutate(cryptic_id = paste0("cryptic_", row_number()), .before = 1)

cryptic_exons

cryptic_exons_gr <- cryptic_exons |>
  select(cryptic_id, seqnames, start, end, strand) |>
  makeGRangesFromDataFrame(keep.extra.columns = TRUE)

p <- ggplot(cryptic_exons, aes(width)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Cryptic exon segment width (bp)", y = "Count")

ggsave(
  file.path(out_dir, "liu_cryptic_exon_width_histogram.pdf"),
  p, width = 6, height = 4
)
```

## Overlap with RepeatMasker

Strand-agnostic overlap, expression of TEs from either strand are interesting
for dsRNA formation.

```{r}
te_hits <- findOverlaps(rmsk_gr, cryptic_exons_gr, ignore.strand = TRUE)

te_cryptic_overlap <- tibble(
  te_id = rmsk_gr$te_id[queryHits(te_hits)],
  cryptic_id = cryptic_exons_gr$cryptic_id[subjectHits(te_hits)],
  overlap_bp = width(
    pintersect(
      rmsk_gr[queryHits(te_hits)],
      cryptic_exons_gr[subjectHits(te_hits)],
      ignore.strand = TRUE
    )
  )
) |>
  power_inner_join(
    rmsk |>
      select(
        te_id, seqnames, te_start = start, te_end = end, te_strand,
        rep_name, class_family, rep_class, rep_family,
        sw_score, perc_div, perc_del, perc_ins
      ),
    by = "te_id",
    check = check_specs(duplicate_keys_right = "abort")
  ) |>
  power_inner_join(
    cryptic_exons |>
      rename(
        cryptic_start = start, cryptic_end = end,
        cryptic_strand = strand, cryptic_width = width
      ),
    by = c("cryptic_id", "seqnames"),
    check = check_specs(duplicate_keys_right = "abort")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    te_width = te_end - te_start + 1L,
    # Fraction of the TE covered by the cryptic exon
    frac_te_in_cryptic = overlap_bp / te_width,
    # Fraction of the cryptic exon covered by the TE
    frac_cryptic_in_te = overlap_bp / cryptic_width,
    te_orientation = if_else(
      te_strand == cryptic_strand, "sense", "antisense"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(te_id) |>
  mutate(
    n_cryptic_exons_overlapping_te = n_distinct(cryptic_id)
  ) |>
  group_by(cryptic_id) |>
  mutate(
    n_tes_overlapping_cryptic = n_distinct(te_id)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  relocate(
    te_id, rep_name, class_family, seqnames, te_start, te_end, te_strand,
    te_width, cryptic_id, cryptic_start, cryptic_end, cryptic_strand,
    cryptic_width, overlap_bp, frac_te_in_cryptic, frac_cryptic_in_te,
    te_orientation, n_cryptic_exons_overlapping_te, n_tes_overlapping_cryptic
  ) |>
  arrange(seqnames, te_start, cryptic_start)

te_cryptic_overlap
```


```{r}
cryptic_exons_annotated <- cryptic_exons |>
  power_left_join(
    te_cryptic_overlap |>
      group_by(cryptic_id) |>
      summarize(
        n_repeats = n_distinct(te_id),
        repeat_names = paste(unique(rep_name), collapse = ";"),
        repeat_class_families = paste(unique(class_family), collapse = ";"),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "cryptic_id",
    check = check_specs(duplicate_keys_right = "abort")
  ) |>
  replace_na(list(n_repeats = 0L))
```

```{r}
te_cryptic_overlap |>
  distinct(te_id, rep_class) |>
  count(rep_class, sort = TRUE)

p <- ggplot(
  te_cryptic_overlap,
  aes(frac_te_in_cryptic, frac_cryptic_in_te)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ rep_class) +
  labs(
    x = "Fraction of repeat in cryptic exon",
    y = "Fraction of cryptic exon in repeat"
  )

ggsave(
  file.path(out_dir, "liu_repeat_cryptic_overlap_fractions.pdf"),
  p, width = 10, height = 8
)
```

## Write output

All tables are written to `data/cryptic_exon_te_overlap/`.

- `lsv_max_junction.csv.gz`: one row per LSV. Holds the dPSI, PSI and
  change probability of the LSV's most changing junction, plus gene, LSV type
  and whether any of its junctions is de novo.
- `cryptic_exons_per_lsv.csv.gz`: one row per cryptic segment per LSV
  exon (many-to-many between LSVs and cryptic segments). An LSV can yield
  several segments, and the same segment shows up once for every LSV that
  contains its exon (e.g. both the source and the target LSV). Use it to go
  from a cryptic exon back to all of its LSVs.
- `cryptic_exons.csv.gz`: one row per unique cryptic exon
  (`cryptic_id`), deduplicated across LSVs. Stats come from the most
  changing LSV (`best_*`), and all contributing LSVs are listed in `lsv_ids`.
  Summarizes the overlapping repeats (`n_repeats`, `repeat_names`,
  `repeat_class_families`); `n_repeats = 0` means no overlap.
- `repeat_cryptic_exon_overlap.csv.gz`: one row per overlapping
  (repeat, cryptic exon) pair (many-to-many). Contains only repeats that
  overlap a cryptic exon, and strand is ignored. A repeat that spans several
  cryptic exons appears once per exon (`n_cryptic_exons_overlapping_te`), and
  a cryptic exon covered by several repeats appears once per repeat
  (`n_tes_overlapping_cryptic`). Includes the overlap in bp, the fraction of
  each element that is covered, and the repeat orientation relative to the
  exon (sense/antisense).

```{r}
write_csv(
  lsv_max |>
    select(-exons_coords),
  file.path(out_dir, "liu_lsv_max_junction.csv.gz")
)

write_csv(
  cryptic_per_lsv,
  file.path(out_dir, "liu_cryptic_exons_per_lsv.csv.gz")
)

write_csv(
  cryptic_exons_annotated,
  file.path(out_dir, "liu_cryptic_exons.csv.gz")
)

write_csv(
  te_cryptic_overlap,
  file.path(out_dir, "liu_repeat_cryptic_exon_overlap.csv.gz")
)
```

## Write to Synapse

```{r}
syn_te_overlap <- synMkdir(
  "syn36639264", "RNA-seq", "Repeats"
)

synStoreMany(
  file.path(
    out_dir,
    c(
      "liu_lsv_max_junction.csv.gz",
      "liu_cryptic_exons_per_lsv.csv.gz",
      "liu_cryptic_exons.csv.gz",
      "liu_repeat_cryptic_exon_overlap.csv.gz"
    )
  ),
  parentId = syn_te_overlap,
  forceVersion = FALSE
)
```
